root_cause.text: In the Thunderbolt XDomain handling code, `tb_xdomain_copy()` always copied `req->response_size` bytes from `pkg->buffer` even when the received control frame was shorter, causing an out-of-bounds read past the valid DMA frame data into stale buffer contents.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `memcpy(req->response, pkg->buffer, req->response_size);` to `memcpy(req->response, pkg->buffer, min_t(size_t, pkg->frame.size, req->response_size));`, and the CVE description states that a short response “reads past the valid frame data in the DMA pool buffer into stale contents from previous transactions.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp the response copy length to the received frame size to avoid copying beyond the packet buffer.
intent_record.what: The function now computes a local size_t variable `len` as the minimum of `pkg->frame.size` and `req->response_size`, and uses that value as the third argument to `memcpy()` instead of always copying `req->response_size` bytes.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the copy operation is limited to the actual size of the received package frame or the available response buffer, whichever is smaller. This prevents reading past the end of `pkg->buffer` when the frame is shorter than the requested response size, while still returning success and setting `req->result.err` to 0.
